claims.v: local baseball coach
claims.quote: The sighting, filmed by local baseball coach Nick Mariana, is believed to be among the earliest motion picture footage of what would soon come to be called an unidentified flying object (UFO).

At 11:29 am on August 15, 1950, Nick Mariana, the general manager of the Great Falls Electrics minor league baseball team, and his nineteen-year-old secretary, Virginia Raunig, were inspecting the baseball field at empty Legion Stadium shortly before a game.

A bright flash caught Mariana's eye and, according to his reports, he saw two rotating bright silvery objects, flying over Great Falls at a speed he estimated to be around 200 to 400 miles per hour (320 to 640 km/h).
Mariana ran to his car to retrieve his 16 mm movie camera and filmed the UFOs for sixteen seconds.

claims.v: saw two rotating bright silvery objects after a bright flash caught his eye

claims.v: two jet fighters passed over the baseball stadium shortly after the sighting
claims.quote: When Mariana and Ms. Raunig both told him that they had seen two jet fighters pass over the baseball stadium shortly after the sighting, Brynildsen felt that perhaps the jets were the objects Mariana had seen and captured on film.

claims.v: first thirty-five frames of his film, most clearly showing the UFOs as rotating disks, were missing
claims.quote: Controversy soon arose when Mariana claimed that the first thirty-five frames of his film – which he said most clearly showed the UFOs as rotating disks – were missing.
